title: Percentile-driven ranking regression detector for embedding-based rerank
creator: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: We see intermittent, customer-specific drops in rerank quality that do not trigger global NDCG regressions. Hypothesis: failures concentrate in the tail of the query distribution and for specific customer prompt sets (short queries / high OOV). This ticket implements a percentile-driven regression detector that tracks NDCG@k and MRR across percentile slices (P10/P50/P90/P99) per-customer and per-candidate-size bucket, with lightweight on-path instrumentation and A/B hooks for canarying model/kernel changes. Goals: (1) detect regressions earlier for high-risk slices, (2) provide per-customer actionable diagnostics and promptset anchors, (3) integrate with existing AB hook framework and alerts in Console.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Detector computes NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR on rolling 7-day windows for percentile slices per-customer; 2) Alerts fire when relative drop > 3% absolute or > 10% relative on any slice and persists for two windows; 3) A/B canary can be started with traffic fraction and the detector surfaces canary delta; 4) Low-cost path added so the detector adds <5ms p50 latency overhead on the rerank request path; 5) Backfill job available to compute historic baselines for last 90 days; 6) Dashboard shows slice-level baselines, drift, and top-k failing promptsets per customer.
notes: Design choices: use percentile slices rather than coarse cohorts to capture tail failures; compute metrics via streaming aggregator (Kafka->Materialized view) to avoid heavy backfill during rollout; use reservoir sampling of candidate sets for long-tail customers to keep storage bounded; default alert thresholds conservative (3% abs) but configurable per-customer. Rollout: internal canary -> opt-in customers -> global.

implementation_plan: 1) Add in-process sampler + metric emission (2 weeks) 2) Streaming aggregator + materialized store (1 week) 3) Backfill job for 90-day baseline (3 days) 4) Console dashboard tiles and alert integration (1 week) 5) Canary run with ~5 internal customers then opt-in beta (2 weeks).
operations_playbook: If alert fires: 1) Look at dashboard slice + promptset anchors, 2) triage via candidate provenance link to PR/experiment, 3) if canary, roll back canary traffic; 4) if global, failover to fallback reranker and open incident with priority P0.
implementation_notes: To keep latency bounded we compute coarse deltas in-process using sampled candidates and maintain exact counts in the streaming pipeline. Use fixed-window 24h windows by UTC for baseline stability. Per-customer thresholds stored in config DB with default fallback.
qa_checklist: 1) Unit tests for percentile assignment and ndcg/mrr calculation; 2) E2E harness comparing offline/online deltas; 3) Load test with synthetic 10k req/s to assert <5ms p50 overhead; 4) Alert firing simulation with injected regressions.
next_steps: Finish PR review, deploy canary to internal traffic, run 2-week internal beta, gather opt-in customer feedback and adjust reservoir sampling rates as needed.
